Context: with the format raise of one-format-raise-horde-later, every issue gets a collision-proof key, so two issues that took one number in two clones are told apart and renumbered at the merge, and numbers are taken over every branch the clone knows; but the same issue leased in two clones before either pushes is only seen after the merge, because Jarl never pushes or fetches by itself (technical critique I4, I5). Options (labels, not the owner's wording): (1) caught at the merge: the record is never mixed, a doubled number is renumbered, a double lease shows to the jarl as a conflict, and the coordinator's brief says to pull before leasing and push right after, so a double lease is rare but possible; (2) prevented: a lease counts only once it is pushed, the coordinator's list shows a lease not yet on the remote and refuses to treat it as held, which needs a reachable remote for every lease. Recommended: (1).

- 2026-11-03 10:16 key 20261103T0838-gntw by unrecorded · 041 evidence · Ruling approval-defined-by-the-loop: Krzysztof, 2026-11-03 (translated from Polish): "1, but it also depends on the loop: whether we iterate locally or on pull requests (to a feature branch, for example). There, other bots may come in, like CodeRabbit or Copilot. As a rule I work only in local mode. The loop should define what an approved issue means." Each loop defines what an approved issue is: which reviewers' approves clear it (a fresh agent, the owner, a bot the loop names) and what must come with them. With no definition, option (1) of a-011 holds: a bot's verdicts are recorded and counted apart, its findings are welcome, and only a fresh agent's or the owner's approve clears. Built today: a profile's done gate already says approve fresh or none, requires-merged and required slots; the definition extends that.

- 2026-11-04 18:18 by unrecorded · asked a-014 (stuck) · Issue 096, after six reviews: should a refused call end with a line that can be run as printed, or always with the command's form with a placeholder to fill in? Today a refusal can print a corrected call that runs (a value in the wrong case fixed, a removed command such as prio or body replaced by field). Six rounds of review kept finding that such a line, pasted, does something slightly other than the call meant: a word lost, a flag with its value dropped, a second call that runs after the first was refused. Options: (1) keep runnable lines and fix this round's findings, with another review round; (2) no refusal ends with a runnable corrected call: every refusal says what is wrong and ends with the command's form and a placeholder (a removed command ends with the field form that replaces it), which removes the whole class and costs the agent one step to fill the value in; (3) keep runnable lines only for the removed commands with the plainest forms (prio, tag with one change) and the placeholder form for everything else. Recommendation: (2).

- 2026-11-04 19:12 key 20261103T1229-sqer by unrecorded · 096 evidence · Ruling refusals-end-in-a-form-not-a-guess: Under autonomy-quality, at the owner's word 'do it so that it is good' and his question 'which is better in quality' (2026-11-04, translated from Polish; he did not choose an option): no refusal of Jarl ends with a corrected call the tool composed for the caller. Every refusal says what is wrong, in a reason that names the caller's wrong word, and ends with the form of the command that does what was meant, with a one-token placeholder from the closed registry for the value only the caller knows; a removed command ends with the form of the command that replaces it (field <ids> Priority <value>). Pasted unfilled, such a line is refused for its placeholder and writes nothing. Why: six reviews of issue 096 each found one more case in which a composed runnable line, pasted, did something other than the call meant (a word lost, a flag with its value dropped, a second call that ran after the first was refused); the class is removed, not another instance of it. Ready commands that carry no guess (a step the caller must take, shown as its own command) stay as commands. The acceptance line 'ends with a ready command or the flag to add' is met by the form with its placeholder. a-014 stays open for the owner's confirmation.

- 2026-11-08 07:55 key 20261105T0950-jdxy by unrecorded · 157 evidence · Takeover, ae94c29: the field-by-field pairing is replaced by one rule. Every review line of the issue, approves and retractions too, and every Reviews entry take part. A pair is one review when one check finds the verdict, the reviewer, the kind the line records, the model, the relay mark, the batch and the text the same, and the day where both have one. An entry is a line's when every pairing with the most pairs pairs the two. The pairings keep the log's order and the file's while one of them places every entry a line fits, read from the most pairs before and after each place, so the cost is the product of the two lengths. Otherwise the file holds its entries out of the log's order or more of them than the lines they fit (a merge resolved by hand), the pairings are those in any order, and a new note says the place told nothing. Either way an entry a line fits goes unpaired only when another line or entry of its reviewer fits as well, so the note that nothing tells them apart is true wherever it is printed. The brief tests hold an oracle that enumerates the histories and every pairing of each one by one.

A note of several lines written by the pinned 6.1.0 driver keeps its log line in the tail once this Jarl retracts it, where release/6.2.1 hides it: the driver logs the first line without the pointer, and noteLineFits takes a line without the pointer only for a note of one line. Notes the driver or 6.2.0 wrote opening with a conflict marker or with ~~, and driver notes opening with # in a section in parts, keep their line as well: those writers wrote them unescaped, and noteLineFits compares the first line as this Jarl escapes it. After a note of several lines from 6.2.0 or this Jarl, a driver note of several lines with the same first line, once retracted, hides the line of the live note and shows its own. Seen with the command lines alone: driver init, new 001, evidence 001 with a two-line text, then retract 001 note-1 with this Jarl; resume --log 6 shows the retracted line on the tip and hides it on release/6.2.1. An independent checker over 15310 histories (notes by the three writers, every set retracted by the tip): the tip is right in 11618 and release/6.2.1 in 7586, the tip is wrong where release/6.2.1 is right in 2326 (510 of them in the order a loop is upgraded), and a live line is hidden in 130. The acceptance asks for the key the log writes, and the log of these writers keeps the first line bare and unescaped; the new tests cover notes this Jarl wrote only. Counts, show and show --full are right in every history. · model claude-opus-5-5
